definitions.explanation: A name by which something is commonly known, as opposed to its official or formal name. Can refer to nicknames for places, laws, organizations, or people.

examples.japanese: スカイツリーは{通称|つうしょう}で、{正式名称|せいしきめいしょう}はもっと{長|なが}い。
examples.english: Sky Tree is a common name; the official name is much longer.

examples.japanese: この{法律|ほうりつ}は{通称|つうしょう}「マイナンバー{法|ほう}」と{呼|よ}ばれている。
examples.english: This law is commonly called the 'My Number Act.'

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{本名|ほんみょう}ではなく{通称|つうしょう}を{使|つか}って{活動|かつどう}しているので、{本当|ほんとう}の{名前|なまえ}を{知|し}らない{人|ひと}も{多|おお}い。
examples.english: He uses a common name rather than his real name in his work, so many people don't know his actual name.

notes:
{通称|つうしょう} refers to the name that people commonly use, as distinct from an official or legal name.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {通称|つうしょう}で{呼|よ}ばれる (to be called by a common name)
- {通称|つうしょう}「...」 (commonly known as...)
- {通称|つうしょう}{名|めい} (common name, alias)

In Japanese legal and administrative contexts, {通称|つうしょう}{名|めい} (commonly used name) has specific significance for foreign residents who may register an alternative name for daily use. Laws and regulations in Japan are often referred to by a {通称|つうしょう} that is shorter and easier to remember than the official title.
